rationale: CoMD is a DOE-ProxyApps molecular dynamics code dominated by a small number of hot, floating-point-heavy kernels (force computation, integration, halo exchange), so heavy control-flow transforms must be applied selectively: FLA and BCF get low RuntimeCost weights so the feature-driven selection suppresses them on hot loops while still allowing them on cold driver/setup functions where they deliver most of the reverse-engineering resistance; SUB is favored broadly because arithmetic substitution is cheap and stacks well with FP kernels without altering semantics; SPLIT and IGV get high weights since they add diversity at near-zero runtime and size cost; IBR sits in the middle, useful on branchy control code but throttled on loop bodies; ICALL is kept lowest because CoMD relies on function-pointer tables (potential/halo exchange dispatch), making indirect-call rewriting the most correctness-risky pass and one whose added indirection yields little diversity over code that already uses indirect calls. Overall the table biases toward low-overhead, high-diversity passes with targeted application of expensive control-flow obfuscation, matching an HPC profile where runtime overhead must stay acceptable.
